Dopamine contributes to learning and wanting Berridge & Robinson (1998); Wood &  Rünger  (2016) ; Schultz et al. (1997); Schultz (2016)

Motivation:  Dopamine helps initiate action and sustain effort toward valued outcomes. Learning:  dopamine response signal reward prediction errors. Familiar rewards evoke smaller responses once predictable. Monkey expecting two raisins but receiving one may show dip in dopamine-neuron activity. Habits:  Dopamine supports habit formation. Disrupting dopamine input to the lateral striatum can prevent habit formation in rats. Dopamine responses can shift from reward to its cue through associative learning. 11 Dopamine and behavior Dopamine contributes to both goal-directed action and habitual behavior. Faure et al. (2005); Mohebi et al. (2019); Rankin et al. (2009); Schultz et al. (1997).

Dopamine contributes to learning and wanting Distinction Careful interpretation Learning Some brief dopamine signals help update reward predictions. Wanting Dopamine can contribute to the motivational pull of cues. Liking Pleasure can remain even when dopamine-dependent pursuit is reduced.
